summary: CLARE is a four-role Qwen3-8B agent for 3D asset tools (text-to-3D, reconstruction, point-cloud editing). An approver decides whether to execute or ask, a summarizer keeps the clarified task as structured state, a programmer writes tool-calling Python, and a feedback provider phrases questions. The approver is LoRA-tuned (SFT/DPO) on about 3,000 trajectories against a Qwen3-8B simulated user. On the authors' synthetic 3D-Clarify benchmark (620 scenarios with injected ambiguity, missing information or mistaken details) it reports 60.4% single-step and 43.3% multi-step success vs 24.4% for the best author-adapted clarification baseline. The paper is not about software development; only the clarification-gating idea transfers.

claims.claim: CLARE-SE-DPO reaches 60.40% single-step and 43.34% multi-step success, more than doubling the strongest baseline (CEP 24.40%)
claims.evidence: Table 2, §6.4: single run, no variance. CLAMBER/CEP/3D-GPT are author adaptations ('not exact reproductions'). The same simulated user (Qwen3-8B) generated the training rollouts and runs the evaluation. Single-turn baselines cannot obtain withheld file paths or parameters by construction.

claims.claim: The pre-execution clarify/execute gate is the main source of the gain
claims.evidence: Table 3 ablation: removing the approver drops SR 48.60 -> 27.67 (single-step) and 27.22 -> 13.06 (multi-step); removing the summarizer matters only for multi-step (27.22 -> 20.28). An internal ablation on the same benchmark.

claims.claim: Multi-turn-reward self-evolution improves success at negligible interaction cost
claims.evidence: §6.6, Fig. 5: SR 48.6 -> 60.4 with +0.07 turns (single-step); 27.2 -> 43.3 with +0.76 turns (multi-step). No train/test split between the ~3,000 training trajectories and the 3D-Clarify scenarios is stated (§6.1, A.4), so the gain may be fit to the benchmark and simulator.

claims.claim: Proactive clarification is the missing key to robust 3D execution
claims.evidence: Success is a verifier score on module name, parameters (LLM similarity for text prompts), input-path validity and output extension (§6.3); actual 3D output quality is shown only in qualitative Fig. 4 examples.

patterns.note: Removing the clarify gate roughly halves success (Table 3), and CLARE beats author-adapted ask-first baselines (CLAMBER, CEP). However, the simulated user reveals hidden parameters only when explicitly asked, missing-information tasks are unsolvable without asking (so non-asking baselines fail by construction), the same simulator trains and evaluates, and the domain is 3D tools with simulated lay users, not developers and requirements.

SFT/DPO on simulated rollouts lifts SR over the untuned base, but no held-out split is stated. DPO made the agent more compliant and worse at contradicting mistaken users (61.8 vs 66.8 SR for SFT on mistaken-detail tasks).
Four-role decomposition; only the approver and summarizer are ablated.

methodology.sample: 620 synthetic scenarios (500 single-step, 120 multi-step) across 5 3D domains, each with injected ambiguity, missing info or mistaken details
methodology.baselines: Zero-shot, few-shot, CoT, ReAct, Reflexion, plus author-adapted CLAMBER, CEP and 3D-GPT, all on Qwen3-8B with the same simulator and turn budget
methodology.models: Qwen3-8B for agent, baselines and simulated user
methodology.variance: None reported; single run at temperature 0.6
methodology.ablations: Without approver, without summarizer; SFT vs DPO; training data 1k-3k
methodology.contamination_controls: No stated separation between training rollouts and evaluation scenarios; identical simulator in training and test
methodology.languages: Python tool-calling code for 3D libraries (not a software-engineering task)

standards.artifacts: Code on GitHub; agent, baseline and simulator prompts in appendix; an unresolved '[Insert Main Section Reference]' placeholder remains in A.4.2

biases.detail: Authors' own synthetic benchmark and simulator used for both policy training and evaluation.
No train/test split stated between the 3,000 self-evolution trajectories and 3D-Clarify scenarios.
Single-turn and ReAct-style baselines cannot recover withheld inputs, so their near-zero SR on missing-info tasks is guaranteed by design.
Qwen3-8B everywhere, including the user simulator.
Single run, no seeds or CIs.
Success measures parameter and path matching, not the quality of the 3D output.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None commercial; authors ship both the benchmark and the top-ranked system

verdict_reason: Off-topic for this KB. It concerns 3D asset-creation tools with simulated lay users, not software development with LLM agents or the developers using them. Even within its domain, the evidence rests on a self-built benchmark where the same simulator trains and tests, non-asking baselines fail by construction, there is no variance and no stated held-out split.
applicability: Does not transfer as evidence for the team. The design idea worth noting for an ask-before-implementing step: a separate gate that decides 'execute or ask' before the expensive action, plus a summarizer that stores the clarified requirements as structured state. The ablation suggests the gate carries the effect, not the question-phrasing prompt. If the harness adds an agent clarification step before specs, evaluate it on real tickets answered by real developers, against a baseline that is also allowed to ask, and count interruptions as a cost.
